findings.claim: The unit ships with a live, undisposed major-severity blind-solvability finding: the pipeline's own blind gate recovered BOTH keys without the passage, and one of the two flags is an explicit within-unit leak (q:2 option B names the mechanism that is q:1's key). The pedagogy stage returned MINOR_FIXES without touching a single option, so the flag has no stage disposition anywhere in the record.
findings.evidence: report.json / verdicts.jsonl, las-b15-003, G-STEM q:1: "WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, with within-unit corroboration. The Swedish name-day custom is generally known for its token-sized gift, and q:2's option B asserts 'Gåvans tak' as an established fact, so D is pickable without the passage. ... Blind pick D." G-STEM q:2: "... B, the only balanced two-clause statement and the canonical key shape for a 'vilket påstående överensstämmer bäst' stem ... Blind pick B." Keys are in fact D and B (key_spread ["D","B"]), so the blind solver scored 2/2. The leak is verbatim on the page: q:1 key D = "Att seden satte ett tak för gåvan." and q:2 key B = "Gåvans tak gjorde det möjligt att uppvakta många, och utan tak blev uppvaktningen ett val." — "tak" appears in exactly one option per question and both are the keys. diff candidates/las-b15-003.json candidates-final/las-b15-003.json shows only passage wording ("i hörnet" -> "på hörnet") and q:1 rationale prose changed; every prompt, option and key is byte-identical to the pre-review draft.
findings.why: Pedagogy's own remit is whether a test-wise student can score without reading, and this is the repairable structural half of that (batch11 shipped a repair whose whole point was breaking a cross-question corroboration, per commit e771817). Not a refutation: the batch protocol carries G-STEM flags rather than killing on them (ASSEMBLY.md 'Flags carried to the fleet and V-FINAL'), the same 'live gate flags with no stage disposition' pattern was recorded at minor severity in batch14's audits, and both items still need the passage for the actual content. It belongs in the adjudication package, named, rather than resting in report.json unremarked.

findings.claim: generator_meta.originality_note states a real-entity result that is false: "ingen bärare av efternamnet Malmryd". Malmryd has real Swedish bearers, and the same tool the generator used (Exa) surfaces them on the first page. The parallel claim for Rimhall ("ingen bärare av namnet Rimhall i något resultat") is likewise contradicted by real bearers outside Sweden.
findings.evidence: Exa, this session, query '"Malmryd" svensk person efternamn essäist författare': Jonas Malmryd (linkedin.com/in/jonas-malmryd-aab64353, 'Tf Enhetchef Mobilitetsutveckling', Göteborgs stad, jonas.malmryd@stadsmiljo.goteborg.se) and Annika Malmryd (linkedin.com/in/annika-malmryd-36586048, 'Enhetschef på Språkcentrum i Göteborg'). Query '"Rimhall" efternamn svensk person': 'RIMHALL, GEORGE HENRY' / 'RIMHALL, GEORGE WASHINGTON' (Pioneers and Prominent Men of Utah), 'Rimhall Jack' (Hill's Charlotte NC City Directory 1962), 'RIMHALL - boy' (Arizona Republic births 1963). Query 'category:people Algot Rimhall etnolog svensk forskare': no bearer of Algot Rimhall; results are unrelated real ethnologists (Alf Arvidsson, Kajsa Kuoljok, Asta Burvall, Elin Franzén). Exact-phrase WebSearch was unavailable to me for the same reason as the generator (session budget 200/200 exhausted).
findings.why: Law 16 itself is NOT breached — the rule is a real same-domain entity with the same name, and there is no Algot Rimhall or Barbro Malmryd, no ethnologist or essayist named Malmryd/Rimhall, and the real Malmryds work in traffic planning and school administration. But the ledger sentence is wrong as written, and batch14's audit format shows the correct shape ('"Prigent" is a real Breton surname ... but no Naomi Prigent'). The metadata is the evidence later audits inherit; a flat false negative in it should be corrected to the surname-exists / full-name-clear form, and 'Algot Rimhall' remains unverified by exact-phrase search as ASSEMBLY.md flag 1 requires.

findings.claim: Two planted_traps labels do not name the actual trap. q:1/C is labelled scope_shift and q:2/C detail_as_main, but neither option shifts scope or elevates a real detail — both assert content the passage flatly contradicts or never states. The rationales concede the mismatch; the metadata does not.
findings.evidence: planted_traps: {"1": {"C": "scope_shift"}, "2": {"C": "detail_as_main"}}. q:1 C = "Att firandet höll sig inom hushållet." against the passage's "Därför kunde uppvaktningen sträcka sig långt utanför den närmaste kretsen." — a reversal, not a narrowing. q:2 C = "Etikettbokens viktigaste råd var att hålla namnsdagsuppvaktningen inom den egna familjen och den närmaste släkten." while the only thing the book is quoted as saying is "en gåva på namnsdagen bör inte överstiga vad mottagaren utan besvär kan ge igen" — a misattribution, not a detail promoted to main point. The rationales admit both hybrids in their own words: "C är scope_shift och vänder dessutom stycke 3" and "C är detail_as_main med en förvrängning".
findings.why: Trap labels are the machine-readable teaching taxonomy the bank is mined on; a distractor filed as scope_shift that is really a contradiction skews the trap census and any future 'which misconception does this teach' analysis. The items themselves are unaffected — both options are correctly unkeyable and the student-facing rationales are accurate — so this is a metadata correction, not an item repair.

findings.claim: The 1934 etiquette book is quoted as verbatim period text but is rendered in fully modern Swedish negation, which the language stage (CORRECTED) did not touch.
findings.evidence: Passage: "I en etikettbok från 1934 sägs det rent ut: ”en gåva på namnsdagen bör inte överstiga vad mottagaren utan besvär kan ge igen”." The framing "sägs det rent ut" plus the quotation marks present this as the book's own words; formal Swedish print of the 1930s would far more typically negate with 'icke' ('bör icke överstiga'), and the essay otherwise takes care with period texture (femtio öre, mjölkbutiken, mellankrigstidens veckopress).
findings.why: Arguable rather than wrong — 'inte' was already in use in 1934 and the book is aimed at a broad readership, which is why G-SPRAK passed it 3/3 and I do not treat it as a defect of the Swedish. Recorded because it is the one place in the unit where a quoted historical voice is indistinguishable from the essayist's present-day voice, and a one-word change ('bör icke') would buy the period marker at zero risk to the item: no key, distractor or rationale depends on the quote's wording.
